## Simple explanation

An evaluation dataset contains examples used to measure how well a model
performs. It should represent the cases and conditions relevant to the
model's intended use.

## Technical explanation

Evaluation data may be divided into validation data for model selection
and a test set reserved for final assessment. Examples require reliable
labels or evaluation criteria, suitable sampling, and controls against
data leakage. For generative systems, a dataset may include prompts,
reference answers, rubrics, or human judgments.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Evaluation results guide model comparison, release decisions, and
monitoring. A biased, contaminated, or outdated dataset can give a
misleading picture of system quality.

## How it works

Define the target population and tasks, collect or select representative
examples, label them consistently, and keep evaluation examples separate
from training. Reuse an untouched test set sparingly, and version datasets
so comparisons remain interpretable.

## Practical example

A classifier's evaluation dataset can contain held-out penguin and
ostrich images from sources not used during training, with labels checked
for accuracy and a split that avoids near-duplicate leakage.

## Common misconceptions

- A large dataset is not automatically representative.
- A test set repeatedly used to tune a model gradually becomes part of
  the development process.
- Evaluation data does not eliminate uncertainty or future distribution
  shift.
